body:
`insight:chokepoint-monopolies` · confidence: verified

Cases: ASML (only EUV supplier; ~22x 2012-24), TSMC (leading-edge foundry; ADR ~24x to $363 and a $2tn market cap by 2026), Nvidia (AI compute; see case_study:nvidia). Pattern: the moat is built in public over 5-10 years of technical risk. Early signals: customers paying to secure supply (Intel/TSMC/Samsung €3.85bn for 23% of ASML in 2012; hyperscalers pre-paying for capacity), competitors publicly slipping (Intel 10nm delays 2016-20, GlobalFoundries exiting 7nm 2018), and rising gross margin despite heavy capex/depreciation. Why under-priced: cyclicality (each still fell -55-60% in 2022), concentration on few customers, and geopolitics (TSMC's Taiwan discount; ASML's China export limits). Notable misses: the strategic investors sold early (TSMC sold its ASML stake in 2015; Intel and Samsung trimmed from 2016), and Berkshire reportedly bought and quickly sold TSMC in 2022 on geopolitical risk [unverified]. Lesson: monopolies at technological chokepoints can be owned through cycles, but size them so the tail risk (export bans, Taiwan) is survivable; buy in the cyclical drawdowns, not at AI-peak multiples.

- **Links:** `case_study:asml-2012-2024`, `case_study:tsmc-2012-2026`, `case_study:nvidia`
- **Sources:** [1](https://asml.com/en/news/press-releases/2012/asml-issues-shares-to-tsmc-in-connection-with-customer-co-investment-program) · [2](https://www.eetasia.com/18101601-intel-reduces-asml-stake) · [3](https://www.digitimes.com/news/a20260225PD231.html)

Flag: CLEAN. The Rahul Bajaj branch (d. Feb-2022) runs Bajaj Auto (Rajiv) and Bajaj Finserv/Bajaj Finance/Bajaj Housing Finance (Sanjiv), with Bajaj Holdings & Investment as holdco. The 2007-08 demerger of old Bajaj Auto into Bajaj Auto, Bajaj Finserv and Bajaj Holdings is a textbook value-unlocking split (Bajaj Finance later a 100x+ compounder). No promoter pledging, high payouts: Bajaj Auto paid Rs 210/share for FY25 and Rs 150/share for FY26 plus a buyback of up to Rs 5,633 cr announced May-2026 (its second in two years), together ~100% of FY26 standalone PAT per one analysis. Bajaj Auto closed control of KTM AG (via Pierer Bajaj AG, ~74.9%) in Nov-2025 after KTM's insolvency -- a capital-allocation bet to monitor, not a governance breach. Regulatory blemish: RBI barred Bajaj Finance from lending under its eCOM and Insta EMI card products (Nov-2023) for KFS disclosure lapses; lifted May-2024. Bajaj Holdings trades at a large holdco discount despite dividends. Note: the Kamalnayan/Shekhar branch (Bajaj Electricals) and the Shishir/Kushagra branch (Bajaj Hindusthan, Bajaj Consumer) are separate groups with different records -- do not transfer this flag to them.

- **red flags:** RBI product ban Bajaj Finance 2023-24 (lifted); KTM rescue risk
- **good conduct:** 2008 demerger, buybacks (Bajaj Auto), no pledges

Flag: CLEAN (mostly-clean on structure). Bharti Airtel is controlled through Bharti Telecom (Bharti Enterprises ~50.56%, Singtel ~49.44%), which held ~40.47% of Airtel in Sep-2025; total promoter group ~50.3%. Minority record: no promoter pledging at Airtel; rights issues (2019 Rs 25,000 cr; 2021 Rs 21,000 cr partly paid) offered to all at the same price; AGR dues paid/managed without seeking a bail-out conversion; Bharti Hexacom IPO (2024) was an OFS by the government's TCIL, not the promoter. Singtel and promoter entity Indian Continent Investment have sold blocks (2025: ICIL ~3.43 cr shares for ~Rs 7,189 cr; Singtel ~0.8% for ~Rs 10,353 cr) -- secondary sales, not pledges. Legal record: the 2G spectrum case -- the Supreme Court (2015) quashed summons against Sunil Mittal; the special court acquitted all accused in Dec-2017. Airtel acquired control of Indus Towers (2024) after Vodafone's sell-down. Watch: Mittal's stated plan (2025-26) for Bharti Telecom to regain 51% of Airtel over a decade (~Rs 1 lakh cr at current prices) implies holdco leverage at Bharti Telecom; a 10-year leadership succession plan has been outlined publicly. Status Nov-2026: no regulator actions against promoters found.

- **red flags:** holdco leverage at Bharti Telecom to raise stake (future)
- **good conduct:** rights issues to all; no pledges; transparent block sales

title: US_INDUSTRIALS_peer_comparison › 2. Scores (same formula as the pilots, auto components and IT)

body:
- Per flag, per snapshot and pooled, all weighted: n known, n fired, precision P(O_fail | F), base rate P(O_fail)
  (known set), recall P(F | O_fail), **lift = precision / base rate**, winners excluded = flagged winners / all
  winners (known). 95% percentile CIs from 2,000 bootstrap draws resampling companies within each stratum.
- **Graded red** if pooled lift ≥ 2.0 **and** the lift CI lower bound > 1 **and** the flag excludes < 10% of
  eventual ≥ 3x winners. **Hard** only if additionally pooled lift ≥ 4.0. Otherwise a **question** for the deep
  dive. Decided on primary O_fail; O_strict, per-snapshot and stratum-D-only results are robustness and do not
  overturn the verdict. S3, S3-India, S2b, S5b and S5-US results are exploratory.
- Known biases stated in advance: (1) renamed/merged IBC companies whose old page is gone (Bhushan Steel, Monnet
  Ispat) and 221 IBBI rows without identifiers fall out — survivorship leak toward *fewer* failures; (2) standalone
  accounts under-flag holdco debt; (3) restated, not as-first-reported, numbers; (4) market-cap-to-sales rounding
  near the size boundaries; (5) BSE suspensions carry no date, so the price-series stop is used as the date; firms
  that stopped trading for unrecorded reasons in stratum X are not failures unless the price fell ≤ 0.2× first;
  (6) both windows contain COVID-2020, and the FY2016 window the 2018–19 IL&FS / NBFC credit squeeze — results are
  shown per snapshot; (7) companies that missed filing by T (common in distress) are out of the universe at T.
